name: JetKVM
description: A tiny, open-source KVM-over-IP device built around a low-cost camera SoC — 1080p60 H.264 video with 30-60ms latency, free WebRTC cloud access, and hardware power control available as separate add-on boards.

USB HID Emulation.comment: Keyboard and mouse emulation over a single USB-C connection

Power Control.comment: Requires a separate ATX or DC Power Control add-on board connected via the expansion port; not built into the base unit

Virtual Media Emulation.comment: The USB device class can be switched to present as a mass storage device

GPIO Control via Web UI.comment: No general-purpose GPIO; only dedicated ATX/DC-power/serial expansion boards via the extension port

Multiport KVM Support.comment: Single-port device with no documented chaining/switching between multiple hosts

PoE Support.comment: Only on a separate PoE hardware variant (IEEE 802.3af), sold at a higher price than the base model

Zero-Config Remote Access.comment: Free JetKVM Cloud via WebRTC with STUN/TURN, works behind restrictive NAT with no port forwarding

Clientless Browser.comment: Browser-based control, no client software required

Open Source Firmware & Plugins.comment: System image, KVM runtime, dashboard, and even the cloud implementation are open source on GitHub (jetkvm/kvm)

Scripting.comment: SSH access via Developer Mode allows full customization

Serial Console Web Gateway.comment: Available via a separate RS-232 serial console expansion board, not built into the base unit

Encrypted Stream (TLS 1.3 / AES-256).comment: WebRTC traffic through JetKVM Cloud is encrypted via DTLS-SRTP

No Subscription (On-Premise Only).comment: Cloud access is free with no subscription; the cloud implementation is also open source and can be self-hosted

What's Included.comment: HDMI cable, USB-C to USB-A cable; power/data splitter no longer included as of shipments from May 2026 onward. The ATX/DC power control board is NOT included and is sold separately

Cloud Access.comment: JetKVM Cloud (WebRTC/STUN/TURN) is free, with no paid tier

Additional Accessories.comment: ATX Extension Board, DC Power Control Extension, and Serial Console Extension are all sold separately

Software Licensing Model.comment: Firmware, dashboard, and cloud implementation are all open source (Go/TypeScript/C) on GitHub

SoC / Processor.status: Rockchip RV1106G3 — single-core ARM Cortex-A7 @ 1.0 GHz
SoC / Processor.comment: Includes a hardware H.264/H.265 video encoder (VPU); originally designed for IP cameras

Onboard Storage.comment: Older units used 16 GB soldered eMMC; current units (as of the April 2026 update) use a swappable microSD card instead

SD Card.comment: 32 GB microSD (as of the April 2026 hardware refresh); user-replaceable if it fails

Capture Chip.status: External Toshiba HDMI-to-MIPI CSI bridge chip
Capture Chip.comment: Exact model number not disclosed by the manufacturer; needed because the Rockchip SoC has no native HDMI input

USB Ports.comment: Used for both power and keyboard/mouse/mass-storage emulation

HDMI Input.comment: Mini-HDMI on older units; full-size HDMI on units shipped after the 2026 hardware refresh

Serial/RS232 Port.comment: Available only via a separate Serial Console expansion board

Expansion Slot.comment: For connecting ATX power control, DC power control, or serial console add-on boards

LED Indicators.comment: Status information (IP, MAC address, cable/connection state) is shown on the touchscreen instead of separate LEDs

Power Supply.comment: The PoE variant also supports IEEE 802.3af Power over Ethernet

Voltage/Power Connector.comment: Warning: USB-C PD chargers with voltage negotiation should not be used — higher voltage can damage the device and voids warranty

PoE (Power over Ethernet).comment: Only on the separate PoE SKU (IEEE 802.3af compliant); the standard version has no PoE

Power Control Interface.status: Separate ATX/DC power control add-on boards via the RJ12/5-pin expansion port
